cases.title: A valid --format exits 0 on every command and echoes the exact format
cases.given: A scratch git repo with branch sdlc/S-001 and no config.json
cases.when: Run name, parse, list and preflight with --format set to sdlc/{name}, sdlc/{name:lower}, feature/PROJ-1-{name}, {name}, a/b/c-{name}-x, ünïcode/{name} and Ärger-{name:lower}
cases.then: Each run exits 0 with one JSON object, ok true, format equal to the input byte for byte, empty stderr, no tree change
cases.actual: 28 runs: exit 0, format echoed unchanged, stderr empty, trees unchanged

cases.title: The CLI verdict on each git-unsafe format equals git, and a refusal carries the reason of git
cases.when: Run the four commands with --format=<f> for sdlc/{name}.., sdlc/{name}.lock, -{name}, --help{name}, /{name}, {name}/, a//{name}, a~/{name}, a^/{name}, a:/{name}, a?/{name}, a*/{name}, a[/{name}, a\/{name}, @/{name}, a/.b/{name}, \x01, \x1f, DEL and a@{-1}{name}; run git check-ref-format --branch on each sample
cases.then: A git refusal gives exit 2, one JSON error that holds check-ref-format, 'is not a valid branch name' and the exact stderr of git. A git acceptance gives exit 0.
cases.actual: All 80 runs agree. 18 formats exit 2 with git's own fatal line in the error. @/{name} exits 0, because git accepts @/S-001. \x1f is refused earlier as whitespace (Python \s). a@{-1}{name} is refused earlier as a stray brace. -{name} and --help{name} reach git as a name, not an option.
cases.specSource: R-017 acceptance (the invalid-ref rejection carries the reason of git check-ref-format)

seeds.title: A git binary on PATH decides the format verdict
seeds.detail: validate_format runs the first git on PATH. A fake git that exits 0 admits sdlc/{name}.. (TC-cli-11). The spec does not pin the git binary. A caller that controls PATH controls the verdict.

seeds.title: Zero-width characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: U+200B, U+200D and U+FEFF are not matched by Python \s, and git accepts them, so a\u200bb/{name} is valid (TC-cli-5). The branch names then look the same as names without them. The spec forbids only whitespace.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F are reported as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python \s matches U+001C to U+001F, so a\x1f/{name} fails with 'holds whitespace', not with the git reason. The verdict is correct; the message names the wrong cause.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner has no option for an absolute python path per run
seeds.detail: PATH tests must build a second runner with cliRunner({ python: <abs path> }), because the default python3 lookup uses the child PATH. A run option would make PATH-isolation cases shorter.
